decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing a declaration form for a binding in modern or legacy JavaScript.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use const for bindings that are not reassigned; use let for reassignment; leave var only when maintaining legacy scope behavior deliberately.
choose_this_when: const for stable binding identity
let for loop counters or reassigned accumulators
var only when a legacy function-scoped/hoisted binding is required and tested
avoid_this_when: Do not use const to imply object immutability
Do not convert var in old code without checking hoisting and closure behavior
specific_checks: Check reassignment separately from object mutation
code_examples_or_scenarios: Refactor var loop callbacks to let only with tests for async callbacks
Keep const object mutation visible with naming/docs

decision_rules.decision_context: Comparing JavaScript values where type conversion may occur.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use === and !==; use value == null only as an intentional null-or-undefined check when both are equivalent for that branch.
choose_this_when: Operands are already normalized
You need to distinguish false/0/""/null/undefined
NaN/Object.is edge cases are handled separately
avoid_this_when: Avoid == when operands can be strings/numbers/booleans/objects from boundaries
Avoid changing existing == without tests if legacy behavior accepted coerced inputs
risk_of_wrong_choice: Changed behavior for nullish legacy inputs
code_examples_or_scenarios: if (value == null) can intentionally catch null or undefined; if (id === Number(input)) requires parse/validate step

decision_rules.decision_context: Representing key/value associations.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use plain objects for fixed-shape records with known property names; use Map for dynamic keys, non-string keys, or collection semantics.
choose_this_when: Map when keys are objects/functions or arbitrary user strings
Object when JSON-like schema and property access are natural
Object.create(null) only for special dictionary cases with ownership care
avoid_this_when: Avoid plain object for untrusted arbitrary dictionary keys without own-property checks
Avoid Map when JSON serialization or literal syntax is primary
specific_checks: Check key types and serialization needs
code_examples_or_scenarios: Configuration object: plain object; cache keyed by DOM nodes/objects: Map

decision_rules.decision_context: Representing ordered data versus named fields.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use arrays for ordered dense lists; use objects for named records.
choose_this_when: Array when index/order/iteration over homogeneous items matters
Object when fields have domain names and missing/present distinction matters
avoid_this_when: Avoid arrays for sparse named data
Avoid objects for ordered sequences requiring array methods
specific_checks: Check whether order or names drive access
code_examples_or_scenarios: Rows from CSV: array of row objects or arrays depending schema; user profile: object

decision_rules.decision_context: Representing unique membership or ordered list with duplicates.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use array for ordered lists where duplicates may matter; use Set for membership uniqueness and has/delete operations.
choose_this_when: Set when uniqueness and membership checks dominate
Array when index order, duplicates, map/filter/reduce, or JSON list output dominate
avoid_this_when: Avoid Set when duplicate counts matter
Avoid array membership scans for large uniqueness-heavy logic without reason
specific_checks: Test insertion order and membership semantics
code_examples_or_scenarios: Selected unique IDs: Set internally, array at JSON boundary

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing object-oriented class syntax or closure-based factory/private state.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use the simplest representation: plain function for behavior, class for constructed objects with shared methods, closure for private state or specialization.
choose_this_when: class when instances share prototype methods and constructor identity matters
closure when encapsulated state or partial application is central
plain object/function when no instance model is needed
avoid_this_when: Avoid class for a one-off namespace
Avoid closure state when reset/testing/lifetime is unclear
Avoid subclassing where composition suffices
code_examples_or_scenarios: Point-like objects with methods: class; memoized helper with private cache: closure

decision_rules.decision_context: Placing methods on prototypes/classes or creating a function per instance.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use prototype/class methods for shared behavior; use instance functions/arrow fields only when per-instance closure state or lexical this is required.
choose_this_when: Prototype method when all instances can share one function
Instance method when it must capture constructor-local variables or be pre-bound
avoid_this_when: Avoid per-instance arrow methods by habit in many objects
Avoid prototype methods that require private closure variables unavailable on instance
code_examples_or_scenarios: Event handler needing bound this may use instance arrow; ordinary domain method belongs on prototype

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing or reviewing module format.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use the module system already required by the runtime/build/test/package boundary; do not mix formats in one file without verified interop.
choose_this_when: ES modules for browser module scripts or modern ESM project configuration
CommonJS for legacy Node package/codebase still configured for require
Adapters at interop boundaries
avoid_this_when: Avoid changing module format without checking package.json, file extensions, bundler, tests, and dependency export shape
Avoid assuming default/named interop
code_examples_or_scenarios: Node script with package type commonjs: CommonJS; browser script type=module: ESM

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing async abstraction or refactoring between them.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use the abstraction exposed by the underlying API; use async/await for sequential Promise flows; wrap callbacks only with tested error and multiple-settle behavior.
choose_this_when: Callback when API is event/callback-native and small
Promise when composing one eventual result
async/await when sequential readability improves Promise code
avoid_this_when: Avoid wrapping EventEmitter/streams as a single Promise unless lifecycle is well-defined
Avoid adding async to public sync API casually
code_examples_or_scenarios: fs callback wrapper must reject on error; network sequence can use async/await with try/catch

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing lazy sequence or fully realized list.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use arrays for small reusable lists; use iterators/generators for lazy, potentially large, or custom traversal; use async iteration for values arriving over time.
choose_this_when: Generator when sequence can be computed lazily
Array when callers need random access, reuse, JSON output, or array methods
Async iterable for chunk/page/stream-style async data
avoid_this_when: Avoid generator for simple fixed data
Avoid materializing unbounded streams
Avoid one-shot iterators where callers expect reusable data
code_examples_or_scenarios: Processing file chunks: async iterable; UI list of selected items: array

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing text-matching approach.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use regex for flat, regular, well-tested patterns; use a parser or manual scanner for nested, ambiguous, security-sensitive, or heavily escaped formats.
choose_this_when: Regex for simple validation/extraction with anchors and negative tests
Parser/scanner for CSV-like quoting, nested parentheses, HTML/JS syntax, complex dates
avoid_this_when: Avoid regex when grammar requires nested structure or meaningful error recovery
Avoid manual parser when standard parser/API exists
code_examples_or_scenarios: Email-like quick filter may use regex; parsing JavaScript or HTML should not use one regex

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing data interchange/storage format for JavaScript values.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use JSON for plain data; use custom serialization/schema when values include Date, Map, Set, Error, BigInt-like needs, cycles, classes, functions, symbols, or prototypes.
choose_this_when: JSON for API payloads and plain configuration
Custom replacer/reviver or schema for non-plain values
Alternative format when binary/cycles/types are required
avoid_this_when: Avoid JSON.clone for arbitrary objects
Avoid custom format when interoperable plain JSON is enough
code_examples_or_scenarios: Date-heavy payload needs explicit ISO/reviver policy; Map internal cache should convert to entries if serialized

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing client-side browser persistence.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use the smallest client storage mechanism that matches data sensitivity, size, lifetime, and current browser support after verification.
choose_this_when: Use in-memory state for transient UI
Use verified browser storage for non-secret, client-owned persistence
Use server storage for authoritative or sensitive data
avoid_this_when: Avoid storing secrets in ordinary client storage
Avoid assuming quota/lifetime/private mode behavior
code_examples_or_scenarios: Theme preference may be client storage; auth secret should not be casually placed in localStorage

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing whether to move browser work off the main thread.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Keep simple UI work on main thread; use worker for CPU-heavy or blocking work that can be isolated behind messages.
choose_this_when: CPU-heavy computation hurts responsiveness
Work can be expressed with serializable/transferable messages
Lifecycle/errors can be managed
avoid_this_when: Avoid worker for trivial code or code needing direct DOM access
Avoid worker when data transfer cost dominates
specific_checks: Test worker error/termination and unsupported values
code_examples_or_scenarios: Mandelbrot-like CPU task: worker; simple DOM update: main thread

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing incremental processing or full buffering in Node.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use buffered read for known-small data; use streams/async iteration for large, unbounded, or incremental data.
choose_this_when: Streams when file/network data may be large
Buffered read when simplicity and bounded size are known
Pipeline helpers where current Node docs support them
avoid_this_when: Avoid streams for tiny one-shot config unless needed
Avoid buffering uploads/downloads of unknown size
code_examples_or_scenarios: Small JSON config: buffered; large CSV upload: stream

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing parallel or external execution in Node.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use worker threads for CPU-bound JavaScript that can communicate by messages; use child processes for trusted external commands or process isolation when deployment permits.
choose_this_when: Worker thread for CPU-heavy JS
Child process for invoking external tool with controlled arguments
Separate process when isolation is required
avoid_this_when: Avoid shell execution with unsanitized input
Avoid workers when serialization overhead exceeds benefit
Avoid either without deployment support
code_examples_or_scenarios: ImageMagick CLI may need child process; pure JS CPU transform may use worker

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing target runtime or reviewing file placement.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Run DOM/UI code in the browser; run filesystem/OS/server code in Node; keep shared logic free of host APIs.
choose_this_when: Browser for user-facing DOM, events, browser storage/networking
Node for files, OS, server HTTP, streams, child processes
Shared core for pure language/data logic
avoid_this_when: Avoid importing Node modules into browser bundles accidentally
Avoid using DOM APIs in Node scripts/tests unless environment supplies them intentionally
code_examples_or_scenarios: Form validation pure function can be shared; document.querySelector belongs in browser adapter; fs belongs in Node adapter

decision_rules.decision_context: Reviewing Google Apps Script projects.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Treat Apps Script as its own operational host; classify server .gs, HtmlService client HTML, triggers, and generated/local tooling separately.
choose_this_when: Use Apps Script services in server-side functions after current docs check
Use browser APIs only in client HTML
Use local Node tooling only as build-time support if project actually has it
avoid_this_when: Avoid assuming Node fs/npm/streams or browser DOM in server-side Apps Script
Avoid current quota/scope/service claims without docs
specific_checks: Current Google docs for every service/trigger/quota/scope
code_examples_or_scenarios: HtmlService form upload needs client HTML handler plus server function; SpreadsheetApp writes belong server side

decision_rules.decision_context: Deciding whether to use syntax/API that target runtimes may not support natively.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use native features when all target runtimes support them; use transpilation/polyfill only when build/test/deploy path is verified.

Transpilation is already part of project and production path matches tests
avoid_this_when: Avoid syntax that build supports but runtime path bypasses
Avoid polyfills that change security/performance assumptions

decision_rules.decision_context: Choosing baseline quality tooling for JavaScript review.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Use formatting for consistency, linting for suspicious patterns/environment rules, and tests for behavior; do not let any one tool stand in for the others.
choose_this_when: ESLint catches JavaScript pitfalls configured for the project
Prettier removes style debate
Jest or other runner exercises behavior and async paths
avoid_this_when: Avoid treating green tests as proof of runtime compatibility
Avoid lint rules not aligned with actual browser/Node/App Script environment
specific_checks: Add tests for risks found in review
code_examples_or_scenarios: A Promise rejection bug needs an async test, not just formatting/linting

decision_rules.decision_name: when not to use Proxy or metaprogramming
decision_rules.decision_context: Deciding whether dynamic traps/descriptors/symbol hooks are worth the opacity.
decision_rules.default_low_complexity_choice: Do not use Proxy/metaprogramming for ordinary data flow. Use it only for a clear library/boundary problem with tests for traps and invariants.
choose_this_when: Proxy solves virtual object, validation membrane, logging, or compatibility boundary
Descriptors/symbols implement a documented protocol
avoid_this_when: Avoid for simple defaults, ordinary validation, or hiding API shape
Avoid if debugger/test coverage cannot observe traps
code_examples_or_scenarios: Use plain function validate(obj) instead of Proxy when call sites can be explicit
